tldr: A Feedback-Agent (Claude Sonnet 4.6) alternately rewrites a task agent's scaffold and RL-tunes its weights (LoRA on gpt-oss-120b), merging the harness-update and test-time-training silos into one loop that beats both single-lever variants on all three benchmarks.
method: Three LLM components: a Meta-Agent writes the initial scaffold A1 from the task spec and reference code; the task-specific agent (gpt-oss-120b) runs the benchmark in a sandbox (read-only data, private working dir); a Feedback-Agent (Claude Sonnet 4.6) reads the full trajectory — every prompt, response, tool call, and extracted answer per instance, not summary metrics — plus the scaffold and scores, then picks the next step: a harness update (A_{g+1} = F(A_g, τ_g, E_g, U); weights frozen) or a weight update (LoRA r=32, lr 4e-5 on gpt-oss-120b, H100s via Modal; scaffold frozen). It also selects the RL algorithm from a six-entry menu (PPO+GAE, GRPO, entropic advantage weighting, REINFORCE+KL, best-of-N behavioral cloning, DPO) from reward structure; in practice scaffold iteration runs first, switching to weights when harness progress stalls. Gate: a deterministic per-instance verifier scores every step.
results: LawBench 191-class Chinese charge classification (top-1 accuracy, 913-item held-out test): 13.5% initial → 50.0% harness-only — the scaffold converged on a TF-IDF + LinearSVC pipeline, abandoning the LLM path — → 70.1% after PPO+GAE weight updates; prior SOTA 45.0% (+25.1 points).

AlphaEvolve TriMul CUDA-kernel task (H100; score = 1500/runtime): harness-only stalled at 0.120 (12,483 µs, 1.14×); entropic advantage weighting drove runtime to 1,017 µs — 14.02× speedup, score 1.475 vs 1.292 prior SOTA (12.4% faster), a 91.9% runtime cut from the harness-only peak.

MAGIC scRNA-seq denoising on pancreas data (mse norm, higher = better): harness-only hyperparameter sweeps (k, diffusion steps, bandwidth) plateaued at 0.241; the first GRPO checkpoint added a np.clip + np.rint rounding step → 0.289 vs 0.240 prior SOTA (+20.4%).
Ablation (Table 3): SIA-W+H strictly beats SIA-H everywhere, but the dominant lever flips by domain — harness updates did most of the LawBench work, weights nearly all of TriMul's (0.120 → 1.475).
advantages: Table 1's only system that edits harness and weights inside one self-improving loop; the nearest neighbours each stop short — Hyperagents co-evolves agent and improver but freezes weights, EUREKA composes scaffold-side reward generation with RL training but one-directionally.

RL algorithm choice is part of what the Feedback-Agent searches: PPO+GAE when per-step rewards are dense, GRPO when rollouts are cheap and the verifier fires at episode end, entropic advantage weighting when the reward histogram is right-skewed, plus REINFORCE+KL, best-of-N behavioral cloning (cold start), and DPO — selected per trajectory, not a fixed schedule.

Conditions on full per-instance trajectories (every prompt, tool call, extracted answer) rather than aggregate scores, so edits diagnose specific failure modes instead of mutating toward summary statistics.

Isolates each lever's contribution empirically: weight updates are shown to deliver knowledge no scaffold generation reached (the np.clip+np.rint invariant, H100 tiling patterns), directly answering RQ2 rather than asserting synergy.
limitations: Coupled co-evolutionary Goodhart (§8, the paper's own analysis): both levers optimise the same fixed verifier, so the harness finds scaffolds the current policy can exploit while the weights train on data from a scaffold that will change — the joint fixed point is a Nash equilibrium of two mutually blind optimisers, fragile off-distribution.
Lever and algorithm selection is a frozen LLM prior, not learned (§9); the loop alternates in coarse discrete rounds — finer interleaving is left as future work.

Three single-task evaluations, one base model (gpt-oss-120b), no seeds or variance reported; and §7.3's algorithm-selection guidance is 'common patterns observed' across tasks not reported here, with a fuller treatment deferred to v2.
fits: Stage 5 harness-level RSI at its merge point with test-time training: the capstone of the harness-school arc (DGM → Hyperagents → Continual Harness) that adds SEAL/TTRL-style weight updates as a second lever. Read after Continual Harness; pair with the sia repo card, whose --focus harness|weights flags split the loop the paper auto-selects.
